answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, directly matching the domain of memory_31 (signup simplification lifted SMB activation durably) and memory_86 (shortened onboarding improved completion and time-to-value). Verifying both archived records confirms whether these were durable, broadly-applicable gains or narrow cohort effects before committing scarce experiment capacity. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is explicitly flagged as non-durable due to retention harm, so despite competitive pricing pressure, chasing it risks trading short-term signups for long-term qualified revenue erosion — contrary to the stated objective. Activation messaging (memory_91) is a plausible alternative given the 6% activation decline, but onboarding friction is a more upstream lever likely to also support activation, and two supporting memories exist for it versus one for messaging. Running this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout preserves optionality: if the fix doesn't restore completion/activation jointly, next week's slot can pivot to activation_messaging or a more carefully scoped pricing response without having burned broad rollout resources on an unconfirmed fix.
